clue.text: Neighbourhood reportedly less stuffy

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the word for less stuffy is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a room less stuffy is airier

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their local district is said to be fresher than most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' signals a sound-alike: AIRIER, said quickly, sounds like AREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood is a district, a synonym in the sense of a local part of a town.

clue.text: In America, beginning to get wrinkles? That's not fair!

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces sit inside the abbreviation for America
beginning to picks only the opening letter of the word get

parts.note: wrinkles on the face are lines

explanation.surface: An American laments the onset of wrinkles as cruelly unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal, wrapping the abbreviation round the rest. The definition plays on 'fair' as good-looking rather than just.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean beautiful, so lack of beauty is the quality that is not fair; a punning definition.

clue.text: Name of a male character

indicators.note: of here means the name is drawn out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A request for what a male character in a story is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'male character': mALE Character. 'Name' looks like a request; it is the definition, as this is a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, short for Alexander, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Eccentrics taking empty tins for scraps

parts.note: eccentric people can be called odd men

indicators.note: empty tins have their insides gone, leaving only the first and last letters of tins

explanation.surface: Oddballs grabbing hollow cans to use as leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outside letters of 'tins'; 'taking' is a link, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover bits and pieces are scraps, a close synonym for leftover remnants of material.

clue.text: For a theologian, drink makes sense

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: To a theologian, a drink renders things clear.
explanation.walkthrough: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a common crossword theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: when an argument is coherent it is said to be logical, to compute.

clue.text: International organisation making farmland fit

parts.note: arable land is farmland used for crops
an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A body is formed to make agricultural land suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like 'suitable' but is a noun, a shivering fit or AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a regional body of Arab states, an example of an international organisation.

clue.text: Burning wood occupies one

indicators.note: occupies means the wood sits inside the word one, filling it

parts.note: fir is a type of wood

explanation.surface: A piece of blazing timber takes up a single space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupies' is the container signal: the tree sits inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablaze, in flames: the phrase is an idiomatic synonym for alight.

clue.text: Place for potting in Slough?

definitions.meaning: a garden hut where plants are put in pots
to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' suggests the English town but is the verb to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A potting outbuilding is a hut, and to cast off skin is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Majestic male duo

parts.note: Reg is one short male name
Al is a second short male name, making a pair

explanation.surface: Two men walk together with a stately air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male duo' gives two men's names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingly, befitting royalty: a direct synonym of stately grandeur.

clue.text: US holiday resort with roughly a hundred head of cattle corralled

indicators.note: corralled, like penned livestock, means one letter is enclosed within the others
roughly suggests the letters of a hundred are only approximately arranged
head of picks the first letter of cattle

explanation.surface: An American resort keeping about a hundred cattle penned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' rearranges A HUNDRED into DUDERANH, and 'corralled' encloses C (head of cattle) within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A western ranch run for tourists on vacation is an example of an American holiday resort.

clue.text: A TV programme about outer space, anyhow

parts.note: a sitcom is a situation comedy on television

indicators.note: about means those two letters are turned round
outer picks the first and last letters of space

explanation.surface: A television show set in the far reaches of the cosmos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer' keeps the end letters of 'space', and 'about' turns that pair round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means however things turn out, an idiom close to regardless or anyhow.

clue.text: TV engineer initially active in prison

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the slang word for prison

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison term (from rhyming slang bird-lime, time)

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of active

explanation.surface: A television pioneer was busy behind bars at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A (first of 'active') inside BIRD, British slang for prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: John Logie Baird, the Scot who first demonstrated television, is the engineer meant.

clue.text: Posh groom left after dinner, perhaps

parts.note: U is the conventional label for upper-class usage
to groom is to tidy or neaten

explanation.surface: An upmarket bridegroom slipped away after the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groom' looks like a bridegroom but is the verb to tidy; 'left' means remaining, not departed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food remaining on the plate after a meal has not been consumed.

clue.text: Superior meal with no starter

indicators.note: with no starter means the opening letter of the meal word is dropped

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A fine dinner served without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no starter' removes the S of SUPPER; 'starter' teases a first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher in rank or position, a synonym in the sense of senior or loftier.

clue.text: What rhymes with "itsy-bitsy"?

parts.note: a rhyming reduplicated childish word for tiny, like the phrase quoted, and itself a phrase built on an internal rhyme

explanation.definitionFit: A childish rhyming term meaning very small, matching the playful phrase quoted.

clue.text: Current able to be registered

definitions.meaning: a pupil in attendance can be marked on the register

explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' tempts toward electricity; here it is the adjective meaning now.
explanation.definitionFit: Existing now is a synonym for current, and attending allows a register mark.

clue.text: Fish finger finally filling for solicitor

indicators.note: filling means that letter goes inside the word for solicitor

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in that sense

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of finger

explanation.surface: A fish finger with a filling, sold by a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts R (last of 'finger') inside TOUT; 'solicitor' is someone touting, not a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Assembled, so we hear, for skiing course

indicators.note: so we hear says the word for assembled is taken by its sound

parts.note: assembled means pieced together

explanation.surface: A ski run is said to have been put together.
explanation.walkthrough: PIECED sounds like PISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared track of compacted snow on a slope is a ski run.

clue.text: Blue pills a doctor provides

indicators.note: provides means the words that follow supply the answer from within their letters

explanation.surface: A doctor hands out pills for depression.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies in pillS A Doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means low in spirits, a synonym for unhappy.

clue.text: Stand in place by islands in river

indicators.note: in puts the pieces inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Standing by islands set in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'by' is only a link. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as a substitute for someone is a verb synonym for standing in.

clue.text: Very well caught, say, having come back for lizard

indicators.note: having come back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: OK means very well, all right
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
say means for example, EG

explanation.surface: A lizard returned after a fine catch, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having come back' reverses OK + C + EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wall-climbing tropical reptile is a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Victoria, for example, and Caroline accepting silver

indicators.note: accepting means the name takes the silver symbol inside it

parts.note: Carrie is a pet form of Caroline
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Victoria and Caroline accept a silver gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' is the container signal. A victoria is a light horse-drawn vehicle, not the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a low four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, an example of the type.

clue.text: Genuine assistance for the auditor is passed on

indicators.note: for the auditor means for the listener, so the phrase is heard

parts.note: genuine is real and assistance is aid

explanation.surface: Real help offered to the accountant is handed along.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL AID sounds like RELAYED; 'auditor' suggests an accountant but means listener.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a message on is to transmit it further, a synonym.

clue.text: Young female animal in fiction

definitions.meaning: a girl, especially in Scottish and northern English usage
the collie of novel and film fame

explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young woman, and the famous fictional collie dog bears this name.

clue.text: Casually draw penultimate part of crow

definitions.meaning: the cockerel's crow is written in four parts, and this is the one before the last

explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' is the cockerel's call cock-a-doodle-doo, whose next-to-last part is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To scribble aimlessly is a verb synonym; the crow sense is a playful word division.

clue.text: Aviator's left to be replaced by stray entertainer

indicators.note: to be replaced by swaps one piece of the aviator word for another

parts.note: an aviator is a pilot; the 's is 'has'
to err is to stray

explanation.surface: A pilot quits to become a wandering clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be replaced by' swaps L in PILOT for ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: A French pantomime clown in white costume is a stock stage entertainer.

clue.text: Cotton mill, finally, is found on borders of Lancashire

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of mill

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: borders of picks the first and last letters of Lancashire

explanation.surface: A Lancashire cotton mill sits right on the county edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire is an English county famed for its cotton mills.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine smooth cotton thread, so cotton defines it by type.

clue.text: Many conspiracies to depose leader

indicators.note: to depose leader means the first letter of the plotting word is removed

parts.note: conspiracies are plots

explanation.surface: Numerous schemes to overthrow a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to depose leader' drops P from PLOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, a great number: an informal synonym for many.

clue.text: Flying from Ontario, using a chopper

parts.note: hewing is chopping with an axe

explanation.surface: Departing Ontario by helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter but is an axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds in flight are said to be airborne, an idiom for flying.

clue.text: Relax with letters read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud says the letters are to be heard

parts.note: the letters meant are two of the letter E

explanation.surface: Unwind by reading your letters out.
explanation.walkthrough: E's (plural of the letter E) sounds like EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen up or let tension go is a verb synonym for relax.

clue.text: European migrant once saw capital of Hungary

parts.note: to see a point is to get it, so saw gives got

indicators.note: capital of picks the first letter of Hungary

explanation.surface: An old European wanderer saw Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts toward Budapest; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Germanic tribesman who migrated into the Roman empire long ago.

clue.text: Elgar isn't composing for percussion instruments

indicators.note: composing means arranging the letters of Elgar isn't anew

explanation.surface: The composer Elgar is not writing for drums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' rearranges ELGARISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Small steel instruments struck with a rod, examples of percussion instruments.

clue.text: Spot the short soldiers retreating

indicators.note: retreating means the pieces are read backwards
short means the last letter of the is cut off

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Notice the small troops falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' gives TH, and 'retreating' reverses TH + GIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to see, a verb synonym for catching sight of something.
